summary: Addresses how the Session Description Protocol can indicate an RTCP port for source-specific multicast sessions, where the existing attribute is already used for the feedback target. It updates RFC 5760 and is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Video streaming sends reports back about quality. This fixes a mix-up over which door those reports should use in a one-to-many stream.

questions: rtcp port in ssm sessions sdp
what is the multicast-rtcp sdp attribute
how to set rtcp port in ssm session
what is the rtcp plus one port rule
subtitle: A new SDP attribute, multicast-rtcp, lets a source-specific multicast session pick its own RTCP port.

tldr.problem: In RTP source-specific multicast sessions, the SDP 'rtcp' attribute already names the Feedback Target, so the session's own RTCP port could only be derived from the 'm=' line with the +1 rule.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the 'multicast-rtcp' SDP attribute, written as a=multicast-rtcp:port, which states the RTCP port of the SSM session directly.
tldr.outcome: Distribution sources can use any RTCP port they want. Without the attribute, the +1 rule still applies. The RFC updates RFC 5760.

today: RFC 6128 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 5760, and the metadata for this page lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Port Ambiguity Problem
sections.content:
The Session Description Protocol (SDP, RFC 4566) has an attribute named rtcp that lets RTP applications (RFC 3550) state an address and port for RTP Control Protocol (RTCP) traffic (RFC 3605).

Consider media senders that send RTP packets to a distribution source, which multicasts them to receivers in a source-specific multicast (SSM) arrangement (RFC 5760). The distribution source also multicasts forward RTCP traffic, such as sender reports and receiver reports or their summaries, in the same SSM session.

In such sessions the rtcp attribute names the address and port of the Feedback Target. So it cannot also name the SSM session's own RTCP port without ambiguity. That port had to be derived from the 'm=' line by the +1 rule, even though RFC 3550 had already lifted the requirement for that rule. This RFC removes the restriction with a new attribute and updates RFC 5760.
sections.eli5: One sign was being asked to point to two different doors at once. This RFC adds a second sign so each door has its own.

sections.title: The multicast-rtcp Attribute
sections.content:
A distribution source may send RTP and RTCP to different multicast ports, or may multiplex them on one destination port (RFC 5761). When it does not want the RTCP port to be one higher than the RTP port, it uses the new multicast-rtcp attribute to name the port it wants. If the attribute is absent, the +1 rule applies, as in RFC 5760.

The syntax is rtcp-attribute = "a=multicast-rtcp:" port CRLF, where port is the token defined in section 9 of RFC 4566. The attribute can be used at both the media level and the session level. Except where the document says otherwise, the rules of RFC 3550 apply.
sections.eli5: If the sender wants the report door somewhere unusual, it writes the door number on a note. With no note, the report door is simply the one next to the video door.

sections.title: An SDP Example
sections.content: In the RFC's example a stream is multicast from a distribution source with source address 198.51.100.1 to group 233.252.0.2, port 41000. The line a=multicast-rtcp:42000 sends the forward RTCP traffic to the same group on port 42000. The rtcp attribute separately names a feedback target at 192.0.2.1, port 43000.
sections.eli5: The video goes to one door, the quality reports from the sender go to a second door, and viewers' own feedback goes to a third address.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The attribute is not believed to add any significant security risk. A malevolent third party could use it to redirect RTCP traffic, but that requires intercepting and rewriting the packets that carry the SDP description, and anyone able to do that could do many worse things, such as changing the addresses and ports used for the media.

The SDP description therefore needs integrity protection and source authentication. The RFC suggests S/MIME for SDP in MIME-typed signaling, HTTPS, or the authentication method of the Session Announcement Protocol.
sections.eli5: Someone who could change your note could change much more than the report door, so the important thing is to make sure nobody can tamper with the note at all.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The RFC registers one new SDP attribute: name multicast-rtcp, long form "Port in the multicast RTCP session", type att-field, usable at media or session level, not subject to a charset. Its purpose is to specify the port for the SSM RTCP session.
sections.eli5: The new sign is added to the official list of signs so everybody uses the same name for it.
